Trace, implement and test: Number To Words

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
class Solution {

    public String numberToWords(int n) {

        String[] ones = {
            "", "One", "Two", "Three", "Four", "Five",
            "Six", "Seven", "Eight", "Nine", "Ten",
            "Eleven", "Twelve", "Thirteen", "Fourteen",
            "Fifteen", "Sixteen", "Seventeen",
            "Eighteen", "Nineteen"
        };

        String[] tens = {
            "", "", "Twenty", "Thirty", "Forty",
            "Fifty", "Sixty", "Seventy",
            "Eighty", "Ninety"
        };

        if (n == 0) return "Zero";

        if (n < 20)
            return ones[n];

        if (n < 100)
            return tens[n / 10] + " " + numberToWords(n % 10);

        if (n < 1000)
            return ones[n / 100] + " Hundred " + numberToWords(n % 100);

        if (n < 1_000_000)
            return numberToWords(n / 1000) + " Thousand " + numberToWords(n % 1000);

        if (n < 1_000_000_000)
            return numberToWords(n / 1_000_000) + " Million " + numberToWords(n % 1_000_000);

        return numberToWords(n / 1_000_000_000) + " Billion " + numberToWords(n % 1_000_000_000);
    }
}
